xp_award.description: #310 story-win XP: when the party achieves a story win or milestone out of combat — solves the mystery, completes the objective, turns the arc — award XP here. The game adds it to the sheet and posts it in chat; state the award in your narration too. Never use for combat victories: the game awards those itself.

items.description: #463 story items: when the story gives the player's character an item (found, gifted, looted, purchased) or takes one away (spent, lost, stolen, broken), set this field to an array of `{"name": "<exact item name>", "quantity": <whole number>, "change": "gain"|"lose"}`. The game updates the character's Inventory; do not narrate receiving or losing an item without setting the field. Otherwise omit it.

damage.description: #610 story damage: when the story hurts the player's character this turn (a failed check's consequence, a hazard, a trap — anything the engine did not already resolve), set this field to `{"amount": <whole number of hit points>, "source": "<short source, e.g. rope burn>"}` and narrate the hurt in `text`. The game subtracts the amount from the character's hit points and posts a damage line in chat; do not narrate the character being hurt or taking damage without setting this field (or requesting a `damage` roll when the amount should be rolled). Otherwise omit it.

campaign_ending.description: #1020 campaign ending: when the campaign's story is complete — its final beat has played, or a limit its rules define has been reached (a story Clock that fills, the final choice taken) — set this field to `{"summary": "<one or two sentences: how the story ended>"}` and narrate the ending in `text`. The game posts the ending, marks the session complete and ends the adventure; put the completion XP in `xp_award` in the same reply. Set it only for the ending itself: never while story beats remain, never for a scene or combat ending, and never for the end of a session when the campaign's story continues in a later session. Otherwise omit it.

tracker_changes.description: #1042 story clocks: when the story advances one of the campaign's clocks this turn (the tick events the campaign's rules and the <story_clock> state name: a node finished, a rest taken, a creature escaped, time lingered), set this field to an array of `{"name": "<clock name>", "delta": <segments>}` — or `{"name": "<clock name>", "set": <segments>}` when a rule sets the clock to a value. The game stores the clock and enforces its limit; the values in <story_clock> are the stored truth, never your own count. The game UI shows the tracker line from them (#1062), so do NOT render a tracker line in your prose. If this reply asks for a roll, the changes land on the roll's result turn — send them again there. Otherwise omit it.

final_beat_reached.description: #1042 final beat: when this turn plays the campaign's final beat — the story reaches the final location or last beat its rules describe — set this to true, even when no story clock has filled. The game then requires the ending on the next turn and ends the adventure if it is still not declared. Set it only for the final beat itself, never while story beats remain. If this reply asks for a roll, send it again on the result turn. Otherwise omit it.
